scope.configDialogHint: Choose the sites and models available to the agent.
scope.classifierModelDescription: Used by "Approve for me" to decide whether tool calls can proceed. If a decision fails, it retries automatically and denies the call if it still fails.
scope.classifierModelUnsetHint: When unset, "Approve for me" uses the model selected for the current conversation to make decisions. Accuracy and cost depend on that model. Choose a model with strong judgment. Faster approval model responses mean shorter waits.
scope.fastModelConfigured: Used for lightweight tasks such as input prediction, session titles, and file summaries.
scope.fastModelUnsetHint: When unset, lightweight tasks such as input prediction, session titles, and file summaries use the model selected for the current conversation, which may increase cost or latency. Choose a fast, low-cost model.
scope.modelFollowCurrent: Not specified (use the model selected for the current conversation)
scope.promptSuggestionDescription: After each conversation turn, your next message is predicted from the context and shown as gray hint text in the input. Press Tab to accept it. This makes one additional model call.
scope.imageEmpty: No image generation models in the system (add an image-capable model to a site first)
scope.imageLoadFailed: Failed to load image generation models
scope.imageSiteUnavailable: No enabled site provides this model
scope.discardDescription: Your changes will not be saved if you close this dialog.
scope.previewEmpty: No sites are configured yet. The agent cannot pick models for now.
scope.imageDialogHint: Choose the models the agent uses to generate images. Sites and models are independent: ticking a model on one site only affects that site; the same model on another site must be ticked separately. Models are deduplicated by name and tried in order: each model fails over across its selected sites, then the next model is tried. Independent of the available models.
scope.imageOrderHint: Adjust the order after choosing models: tried from top to bottom; the next one is used only after the previous fails everywhere.
